content: Fluconazole is a medication prescribed to treat fungal infections, including yeast infections of the vagina, mouth, throat, esophagus (the tube connecting the mouth to the stomach), abdomen (the area between the chest and waist), lungs, blood, and other organs. It is also used to treat fungal meningitis, which is an infection of the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord. Additionally, fluconazole is used to prevent yeast infections in patients undergoing chemotherapy or radiation therapy before a bone marrow transplant. This medication belongs to a class of antifungals called triazoles, and it works by inhibiting the growth of fungi responsible for infections. Fluconazole is available as a tablet or a liquid suspension to be taken orally, usually once a day. Depending on the condition being treated, you may need to take a single dose or continue treatment for several weeks or longer. The duration of treatment depends on the severity of your condition and your response to the medication. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take fluconazole exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Your doctor may recommend a double dose on the first day of treatment. Shake the liquid form well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Continue taking fluconazole until your doctor advises you to stop, even if you feel better. Stopping the medication too soon may result in the recurrence of the infection. Fluconazole is sometimes used to treat severe fungal infections that originate in the lungs and spread throughout the body, as well as fungal infections of the eye, prostate, skin, and nails. It may also be prescribed to prevent fungal infections in individuals with HIV, cancer, or those who have undergone organ transplant surgery. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication with your doctor. Before taking fluconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fluconazole, other antifungal medications (such as itraconazole, ketoconazole, or voriconazole), or any other drugs. Do not take cisapride while using fluconazole. Additionally, inform your doctor about all other medications you are taking, including antibiotics, diabetes medications, anticonvulsants, immunosuppressants, and others, as fluconazole may interact with them. Let your doctor know if you consume large amounts of alcohol or have a history of cancer, AIDS, irregular heartbeat, or heart, kidney, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking fluconazole, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you can continue your normal diet while taking fluconazole. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Fluconazole may cause side effects. Common side effects include headache, dizziness, diarrhea, stomach pain, heartburn, and changes in taste perception. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include upset stomach, extreme fatigue, unusual bruising or bleeding, lack of energy, loss of appetite, pain in the upper right abdomen, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, dark urine, pale stools, seizures, rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, or extremities, and difficulty breathing or swallowing. If you experience any of these serious side effects, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store fluconazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Discard any unused liquid medication after 14 days. Consult your pharmacist about proper disposal of unused medication. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include hallucinations or extreme fear that others are trying to harm you. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may order tests to monitor your response to fluconazole. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the medication, contact your doctor.
